the recovery of fatigued muscle fibres is affected by changes of the extrellular tonicity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the fatigue resistance inXenopus muscle.
the regulation of the contractile apparatus of muscle cells by the extracellular environment and the intracellular ionic environment.
the mechanism of the postcontractile depression of force (PCD) in isolated frog muscle fibres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PCD is caused by a reduced ability of fatigued fibre to respond to an increased extracellular tonicity.
the PCD is due to a reduced Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmicreticulum during the recovery period after fatigue.
the sensitivity of the signal transmission is altered during fatigue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PCD is caused by an increased Ca2+ efflux from the sarcoplasmicreticulum, and that this increased efflux is caused by a reduced Ca2+ binding capacity of the sarcoplasm.
the PCD is a result of a reduced signal transmission from t-tubule to sarcoplasmic membrane.

PCD is caused by a failure of the calcium-release channels to respond to the depolarization of the t-tubules during the recovery period, and this failure is more pronounced in type 1 than in type 2 fibres.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extracellular tonus is an important factor in the control of force production in muscle fibres.
the extracellular tonicty can be used to modulate the force output in fatigued muscle fibres.
the extracellular environment has a major influence on the recovery process.
